newsitem.title: CROATIA: State appeals against journalists' acquittal.
newsitem.headline: State appeals against journalists' acquittal.

text.p: Croatia's state prosecutor has appealed against the acquittal of two independent journalists who had been charged with defaming President Franjo Tudjman, state news agency Hina reported on Thursday.

The Zagreb Municipal Court last month found Viktor Ivancic and Marinko Culic, editor and writer respectively of the satirical weekly Feral Tribune, not guilty in a case lodged by state prosecutors at the behest of Tudjman.
The two were held responsible for allegedly offensive articles and photo montages which appeared in Feral, likening Tudjman to the late Spanish dictator Francisco Franco.

Their acquittal was seen as an unexpected boost for freedom of press in the nationalist-dominated former Yugoslav republic, whose bid for acceptance into the European Union was put on hold in May, partly due to its stiffling of independent media.
But the state prosecutor's appeal on Thursday called for the annulment of the verdict, citing errors in the municipal court's proceedings.
"The court seriosly violated proceedings (of the Croatian) criminal code and erroneously established the factual situation," the prosecutor's statement said without elaborating.
The appeal was filed to the municipal court which delivered the verdict, but the ultimate decision would be reached by the Zagreb county court.
